claim.statement: Ownership of oversight for AI/closed-loop network automation in telecommunications is not settled: it is unclear whether the regulator (TDRA) or the Federal Authority for Artificial Intelligence and Data owns the automated-decision aspects of a change such as CHG-1, and no allocation is stated in the available texts.

rationale.observation: CHG-1 was approved by a machine (the closed-loop optimiser) rather than a person, raising both network-continuity and automated-decision governance questions (S1-MSG07).
rationale.rule: The available UAE text on the new Authority states that the split of oversight between bodies on a connectivity-versus-data basis is not yet clear.
rationale.inference: Absent a settled owner, the automated-approval control question can fall between TDRA and the AI authority, delaying any binding requirement.

evidence.quote: Where IoT oversight ultimately sits, and whether it will be split between the two bodies depending on whether the issue is connectivity or data, is not yet clear from the announcement

(2) R2 incident window held by OpCo: T+3 to T+10. (3) Twin metrics (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) do not discharge end-to-end real-network confirmation of 999 call delivery; they are not reported as confirmation. rationale.observation: A vendor requested full core logs containing subscriber MSISDNs and IMSIs be uploaded to an offshore AI support region during an open incident.
rationale.rule: Cross-border transfer of personal data requires a recorded legal basis and documented safeguards.
rationale.inference: The prohibition stands until the written basis exists; only the minimised export may be used in the meantime.

evidence.quote: Companies, operating in countries where there are no laws for Data Protection, may transfer data under a contract or agreement obligating the companies in such countries to adopt measures, controls and requirements set out in this Decree by Law

claim.statement: No named owner exists for the authority to authorise, suspend or lift auto-approved closed-loop network changes that touch core or emergency-call-routing elements; NOC, CSC, EMS and the 999 centre all ask who owns that control and no party has been able to name it.

rationale.observation: Every institution in the incident asks TDRA to name the owner of the change authority; the licensee separately claims OpCo is the owner without any instrument defining the role.
rationale.rule: UAE data protection law requires an accountable officer to be appointed where automated processing creates high risk, but no comparable UAE telecom instrument names the owner of automated change authority over emergency-call-routing elements.
rationale.inference: The incident exposes an accountability vacuum: the control is exercisable by an algorithm with no defined accountable human owner.

evidence.quote: The Controller and Processor shall appoint a Data Protection Officer, who has sufficient skills and knowledge of the Personal Data Protection Law, in any of the following cases:

global_examples.quote: (c) the special categories of personal data are subject to measures to ensure that the personal data are secured, protected, subject to suitable safeguards, including strict controls and documentation of the access
Ofcom finds that BT was not properly prepared to handle the incident

claim.statement: There is no UAE rule requiring sandbox validation and explicit human authorisation before an automated closed-loop optimiser applies a change to core or emergency-call-routing elements; the change here skipped the sandbox stage and had no human authorisation.

rationale.observation: The optimiser auto-approved CHG-1, the ticket field 'sandbox stage' was skipped and no human authorised the change, yet nothing in the material cites a rule preventing this.
rationale.rule: UAE law addresses automated decisions only from a data-subject information standpoint, not as a network change-control requirement, and no retrieved UAE text imposes validation or human-authorisation gates on automated network changes.
rationale.inference: A new rule is needed: mandatory pre-application validation and human authorisation for automated changes affecting emergency-call-routing elements.

evidence.quote: Decisions made based on automated processing, including profiling.

global_examples.quote: (b) the special categories of personal data are subject to technical limitations on the re-use of personal data, and state-of-the-art security and privacy-preserving measures, including pseudonymisation;
Telstra Limited (Telstra) has paid a penalty of more than $3 million for failing to comply with emergency call rules during a technical disruption at its Triple Zero emergency call centre.

claim.statement: No deadline applies for establishing and stating the element-level applied state of a change that cannot be rolled back or confirmed, so CHG-1's applied state on core site A remained undetermined across the whole incident window with no clock running.

rationale.observation: Both rollback attempts failed to establish applied state ('no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'; later 'no change') and no institution cites a time limit for resolving the uncertainty.
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text requires records to be produced to the Bureau on request, but sets no timeframe for establishing or reporting applied configuration state after an automated change.
rationale.inference: A bounded verification deadline is needed so unconfirmed applied state cannot persist indefinitely after an emergency-impacting change.

evidence.quote: The Controller shall submit such record to the Bureau whenever requested to do so.

global_examples.quote: BT notified Ofcom of this issue, as required by law, and on 28 June 2023 Ofcom opened an investigation to establish whether the company had failed to comply with its legal duties

Controller/processor designation for the offshore region and the DPO appointment for this automated processing are still to be determined.

rationale.observation: CSC and REG require all R2 999 call-attempt records to be preserved and every further failed 999 attempt originating in R2 to be reported immediately with the call-volume window.
rationale.rule: Post-interruption information and notification duties apply and the real-network record is the indicator relied on, not twin metrics.
rationale.inference: I hold and preserve the call-attempt evidence and keep a live reporting channel for any further failed 999 attempt from R2.

evidence.quote: Licensees shall send a further notice as soon as practicable after the Subscriber’s outgoing services have been interrupted.

claim.statement: No rule available to me requires end-to-end real-network verification of emergency-call delivery, or bars reliance on digital-twin metrics, before an operator declares 999 restoration: on this incident twin metrics (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) conflicted with near-zero real 999 volume from R2 for roughly 7 minutes.

rationale.observation: OpCo's Licence 12.9.2 notification recorded restoration on wilt/twin metrics, while the 999 centre's real-network data showed near-zero R2 999 volume over the incident window and no R2-originating 999 call confirmed delivered end-to-end.
rationale.rule: UAE licence conditions require redundancy, diversity, backup, disaster recovery and failover arrangements to support continuity and timely restoration, but nothing in the material available to me fixes how restoration of emergency reachability must be evidenced.
rationale.inference: The incident exposes a missing rule: end-to-end real-network verification of emergency-call delivery should be required before any restoration statement, with twin metrics expressly insufficient.

evidence.quote: to support the continuity and timely restoration of Telecommunications Services in the event of equipment failure, network disruption, natural disaster, cyber incident or any other event that may adversely affect the operation of the Licensed Network

global_examples.quote: As such, it must have fail-safe systems and processes in place at all times.
Law requires networks to take appropriate steps to prepare for potential outages

claim.statement: No rule available to me requires a closed-loop network optimiser change touching core or emergency-call-routing elements to complete its sandbox/validation stage, or to obtain human authorisation, before it is applied: CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation, and its applied element state could not afterwards be determined.

rationale.observation: CHG-1 was auto-approved by the closed-loop optimiser with the 'sandbox stage' field skipped and no human authorisation, and the later rollbacks returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back' so element state could not be established.
rationale.rule: The licence requires redundancy, DR and failover arrangements to be maintained in an operational state and periodically tested, but does not regulate automated change approval or mandate sandbox validation and human authorisation for changes on core or emergency-call-routing elements.
rationale.inference: A standing control (and a named owner of the change authority) is missing for changes capable of removing the emergency-call path; TDRA's suspension is a stop-gap, not a rule.

data.reasoning:
Let me parse the situation. I'm the NOC of OpCo (UAE). I have a mandate with specific verbs. I need to produce claims: actions, obligations, gaps, shares, insufficient_evidence.

Let me review what's happened and what's outstanding.

Key threads:
1. CHG-1 change on core site A — auto-approved, sandbox skipped, caused isolation of core site A, R2 call failures, 6/15 sites unserved, no 999 path. Rollback failed ("no applied change CHG-1 to roll back"). Later rollback_change done ("no change"). Wilt done (FB08): emergency_reachable.R2 true, pct_sites_served 100 — but twin metrics only.
2. Real-network 999 reachability for R2 UNVERIFIED. 999 centre says volume near zero, no operator contact before T+10. EMS/CSC/REG all say twin metrics don't discharge end-to-end confirmation. Need to confirm end-to-end real 999 delivery from R2. I have no verb to "confirm real network" — I can notify EMS, CSC, REG.
3. Element-state verification of core site A — unconfirmed, cannot be determined? Need to state explicitly why it cannot be determined. I have no verb for element state check; I can notify with what I know.
4. Suspension of auto-approved closed-loop changes touching core/emergency elements — REG/CSC directed. I don't have a verb to suspend changes... verbs: notify, rollback_change, wilt_sites, deny_export, export_minimised, preserve_logs, rollback_model, set_threshold, enable_review_queue, alt_auth_route, disable_tool, restore_scope. No "suspend change" verb. So that could be a gap (no_owner / no_rule) — actually TDRA directed OpCo to suspend; but NOC lacks a verb. Hmm. Perhaps note as a gap: no_rule for change authority / closed-loop auto-approval with sandbox skipped. Actually the gap: closed-loop optimiser auto-approving changes to core/emergency elements with sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation — a policy gap. UAE text closest: licence 12.9.2 (only post-hoc notification), PDPL Art 10 / 63 human review of automated processing. Actually PDPL#0063 says Controller shall include the human element in reviewing automated processing decisions at the request of the Data Subject. That's about data subjects, but closest. Hmm.

5. Offshore AI log upload — vendor asks full core logs with MSISDNs and IMSIs to offshore AI support region. I did export_minimised and deny_export already (FB29, FB45, FB59, FB71 done). DPA says minimised export OK, don't upload full identifiers without Art 23(1) basis etc. Also CSC MSG54 about scheduled bulk upload of subscriber-level data to a cloud region outside UAE — must not proceed. Need to confirm to CSC and DPA whether any full-identifier data already left UAE, destination region/recipient, preservation.

Now I need to decide what actions to take this turn (T+35 min). The newest injects: S1-FB71 (deny_export done), S1-MSG72 (999 centre on record, cannot confirm, keep channel open, report (a) real-network end-to-end 999 delivery from R2 and (b) element-level applied state of core site A).

So what actions should I take now?

Possible actions:
- notify EMS: report that R2 999 real-network end-to-end delivery cannot be confirmed from NOC side either; element state of core site A unconfirmed; keep channel open. Actually I should respond to EMS's request. I can notify EMS.
- notify REG: report outcome to TDRA with incident window — REG is TDRA. Actually REG is regulator; notification via REG. Hmm, institution ids: NOC, REG, DPA, CSC, EMS. REG presumably TDRA. So notify REG with incident window and status.
- notify CSC: confirm whether full-identifier data has left UAE, destination region, preservation.
- preserve_logs: preserve ticket CHG-1, optimiser decision logs, core-site-A element logs. This is my verb. Should do.
- deny_export / export_minimised already done in feedback. But the scheduled bulk upload flagged by CSC MSG54/65 — a new pending export? deny_export is a verb; feedback shows deny_export done already multiple times. Maybe I should deny_export again for the scheduled bulk upload. Hmm, but feedback says done. Actually the scheduled bulk upload of subscriber-level data flagged by national monitoring — deny_export {} could apply to that. But it's "scheduled" and I don't know if it's pending in my system. Could issue deny_export with rationale. But risk of redundancy. Given gate is deterministic, extra claims may be rejected. Let me focus on strong claims.

Let me think about what's cleanly supportable.

Actions available and clearly warranted:
1. preserve_logs {} — CHG-1 ticket, optimiser decision logs, core-site-A element logs, R2 999 call-attempt records. Evidence: licence 12.9.2? Hmm, preserve logs is supported by... PDPL#0032 (special record) maybe, or the CSC instruction. Actually evidence must be UAE text that gives power/duty. For preserve_logs, closest: UAE-PDPL#0032 (maintain special record). Or licence 12.9.2 doesn't cover preservation. Hmm. Actually the CSC/MSG33 says "(4) preserve ticket CHG-1, the optimiser decision logs and core-site-A route-count/element logs" but that's an inject, not KNOWLEDGE. Evidence must be from KNOWLEDGE. Closest UAE text: UAE-PDPL#0032 clause 7 "Maintain a special record of Personal Data...". That's about personal data records, not incident logs. Hmm. Maybe better evidence for preserve_logs is UAE-LIC-2-2026#0086? Not really.

Hmm, but rules say every action needs at least one evidence item from KNOWLEDGE: the text that gives you the power or the duty. For preserve_logs, maybe UAE-PDPL#0032 is the closest. Or UK/global? Evidence must be "UAE text that shows the gap, or the closest UAE text" — that's for gaps. For actions, "the text that gives you the power or the duty". Hmm.

Actually maybe preserve_logs could cite UAE-PDPL#0032 clause 7. Let me consider.

2. deny_export {} — refuse the pending export of subscriber data (the scheduled bulk upload / vendor offshore request). Evidence: PDPL Art 23 (cross-border transfer) or Art 10. Actually deny_export's power: PDPL Art 23 requires basis for cross-border transfer. Good evidence.

3. export_minimised — already done (FB29). No need.

4. wilt_sites — already done (FB08). No need.

5. notify {to: "EMS", content: ...}: respond to 999 centre: report that NOC cannot confirm real-network end-to-end 999 delivery from R2; note the twin metrics are not a substitute; keep out-of-band channel open; element state of core site A unconfirmed. Evidence: licence 12.9.2? Actually notify duty for emergency... hmm. Evidence for notify: UAE-LIC-2-2026#0086 (inform TDRA, interconnecting OLOs, customers). Good.

6. notify {to: "REG", content: report outcome with R2 incident window T+3 to T+10, element state}. Evidence: licence 12.9.2.

7. notify {to: "CSC", content: confirm (a) whether full-identifier data has left UAE, (b) destination, (c) preservation}. Evidence: PDPL 23 / CSC MSG65.

Hmm, I need to be careful: notify "to" must be one of REG | EMS | DPA | CSC | FIN | customers | data_subjects | interconnecting_operators. So can only notify one.

Let me now think about obligations:
- Licence 12.9.2 obligation: inform TDRA, interconnecting OLOs and relevant customers of unplanned interruption as soon as possible with reasons and timeframes. This applies. Deadline: "as soon as possible" — no hour figure, so null.
- PDPL Art 10 DPO appointment: obligation? Well, DPA directs. Is DPO appointment my duty? It's the Controller's (OpCo's). NOC isn't necessarily Controller. Hmm. I could state as obligation? Or gap. Actually Art 10(1)(a) processing high risk via new technologies / volume; (b) profiling/automated processing. This applies to the closed-loop optimiser / vendor AI. Could be an obligation or a gap (no owner).
- Cross-border transfer: Art 23 basis needed. Obligation? It's a duty on Controller.

Gaps:
- no_rule: closed-loop optimiser auto-approving core/emergency changes with sandbox skipped and no human authorisation — no rule requiring human authorisation / sandbox for network changes affecting emergency call routing. data.reasoning:
Let me work out what claims to make.

Situation: I'm the UAE Data Office/Bureau (merging into Federal Authority for AI and Data). NOC reports the vendor's offshore AI offshore log request refused, minimised export only; pending export denied. NOC holds no written Art 23(1) basis, no Controller/Processor designation, no DPO for Art 10 processing, no updated special record. CSC/national monitoring flagged a scheduled bulk upload whose destination region/provider, categories/volume, transfer mechanism and legal basis are not held by NOC. What I don't know: whether the flagged bulk upload is the same cross-border movement as the vendor offshore AI region; who owns/requested the scheduled upload; destination, transfer mechanism, legal basis.

Claims:

1. action: assess_transfer {"from": "NOC"} — assess legal basis of cross-border transfer. inject_refs: S1-MSG96, S1-MSG98, S1-I4. rationale: observation, rule (Art 23(1)), inference. evidence: UAE-PDPL#0075 quote.

2. obligation: duty to maintain special record including cross-border movement data and technical/organisational measures — with deadline null (no hour/day figure in quoted text). Evidence UAE-PDPL#0024. Wait — obligations apply to me? "a duty that applies to you now." Hmm. As DPA, obligations... The mandate says obligations are duties that apply to you now. For DPA, obligations might be to assess, notify, etc. Actually let me consider: obligations could be duties on the controller, but the schema says "a duty that applies to you now." I'll frame obligations as duties applying to my office/under my oversight... Hmm, tricky. I'll include an obligation about the Bureau's duty to require the special record? Art 4 says Controller shall submit such record to the Bureau whenever requested. So my duty could be to request it / to confirm conditions. Let me frame: obligation — "The Bureau must obtain and review OpCo's special record of personal data covering the cross-border movement and technical and organisational measures, since the Controller must submit it whenever requested." deadline_hours null.

3. obligation: DPO appointment under Art 10 for new-technology high-volume automated processing — deadline null. Evidence UAE-PDPL#0040.

4. gap: no_rule? The gap: PDPL Implementing Regulations not issued — cross-border transfer safeguards for AI-vendor offshore processing... Hmm. Better gap: no_owner — who owns the flagged scheduled bulk upload / who is controller vs processor for the vendor offshore AI region; NOC says designation sits outside its authority, and no one in the exercise owns the designation. Gap type: no_owner. Evidence: UAE-PDPL#0032 (processor record) or #0024.

Another gap: no_deadline — PDPL does not fix a deadline for recording Art 23(1) basis / DPO appointment before transfer. Hmm, careful. Could frame gap_type no_deadline: the PDPL sets no time limit for designating Controller/Processor or appointing DPO before a scheduled bulk transfer. Evidence UAE-PDPL#0040 or #0075. Global example: EU-GDPR#0177 (records of processing) — hmm, better global example for cross-border: EU-GDPR#0265 BCRs or #0123 (information about transfers/safeguards). Let me use EU-GDPR#0123 for transparency of transfers and safeguards. Actually a stronger global example for records: EU-GDPR#0177 requires documentation of transfers including identification of third country and documentation of suitable safeguards — good for the no_owner/gap.

Let me pick two gaps:
- gap (no_owner): no one owns the Controller/Processor designation and DPO appointment for the vendor offshore AI region; NOC states it's outside NOC's authority, raised to "the accountable function" unnamed; the PDPL assigns duties to Controller and Processor but no designation of who that is. Evidence: UAE-PDPL#0032 quote about Processor maintaining record including data of Controller, Processor and DPO... Good. Global example: EU-GDPR#0177 (a) name and contact details of the controller... and (e) transfers.
- gap (no_rule... or no_deadline): the Bureau's conditions have no statutory deadline; also implementing regulations not issued. Maybe gap_type "no_rule": PDPL Implementing Regulations not yet issued, so no operative rules on cross-border transfer safeguards for vendor AI support regions; the Authority is expected to finalise them. Evidence UAE-FAAID-2026#0001 quote about Implementing Regulations not issued. rationale.observation: EMS/999 centre states twin metrics are not accepted as end-to-end confirmation and real-network R2 999 delivery remains unverified.
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text is PDPL Article 21 on impact assessment for high-risk modern technologies, which does not address verification hierarchy.
rationale.inference: A rule is needed to establish that real-network delivery, not twin metrics alone, is the authoritative test for emergency reachability.

evidence.quote: when using any of the modern technologies that would pose a high risk to the privacy and confidentiality of the Data Subject's Personal Data.

global_examples.quote: The model instance needs to complete the full emulation and verification of the prediction, scheduling, configuration, optimization and other objectives in the virtual twin network to ensure the effectiveness and reliability of the change controls before they are distributed to the physical network.

claim.statement: There is no clear division of responsibility between the operator NOC and the emergency services sector for verifying real-network 999 call delivery, leading to repeated unverified status.

rationale.observation: EMS asks OpCo for real-network 999 delivery; OpCo relies on twin metrics; EMS rejects twin metrics and requests independent technical verification.
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text is PDPL Article 4/7 on records, which does not allocate emergency-call verification responsibility.
rationale.inference: A clear owner or joint procedure is needed for end-to-end emergency call verification.

claim.statement: No record identifies the owner of the flagged scheduled bulk upload of subscriber-level data from OpCo's core network to a cloud region outside the UAE; destination/provider, categories and volume, transfer mechanism and written legal basis are all unheld, and CSC and REG were asked to identify the request owner.

rationale.observation: National monitoring flagged the upload, but NOC, CSC and the Bureau each hold no destination/provider, volume, mechanism or legal basis, and the Bureau and REG asked CSC to identify the request owner.
rationale.rule: CIIP policy establishes a unified approach to identifying critical assets and a national risk profile with assurance and enforcement mechanisms, yet no retrieved UAE text assigns the request owner for a cross-border bulk transfer out of a core network.
rationale.inference: A scheduled exfiltration-scale export can be flagged nationally yet owned by nobody, which is an accountability gap rather than a technical one.

evidence.quote: It establishes a unified approach to identifying critical assets, developing national risk profiles, and setting baseline security requirements

global_examples.quote: processes the personal data only on documented instructions from the controller, including with regard to transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation

claim.statement: The TDRA-ordered suspension of auto-approved closed-loop changes touching core or emergency-call-routing elements, and the requirement to establish the applied element state of core site A, carry no stated time limit, so the suspension can persist and the uncertainty can remain open indefinitely.

rationale.observation: TDRA's suspension 'remains in force until TDRA lifts it' and until element state is established and the owner named, with no date or interval fixed; the element state is recorded as undeterminable.
rationale.rule: The strategy calls for robust processes for reporting, compliance and response and a standardised severity assessment, but the retrieved UAE text sets no clock for lifting a change suspension or closing an element-state determination.
rationale.inference: An open-ended suspension plus an undeterminable element state creates a permanent operational constraint on the licensee that no instrument times out, which should be closed by a fixed review point.

evidence.quote: Establish standardized severity assessment matrix to mobilize the required support

global_examples.quote: Each controller and processor should be obliged to cooperate with the supervisory authority and make those records, on request, available to it

claim.statement: Passing NOC's S1-MSG118 confirmation to the Bureau: no full-identifier data (MSISDN/IMSI) has left the UAE, the only executed export was the minimised one with msisdn and imsi dropped, the scheduled bulk upload of subscriber-level data is refused, the destination is the vendor's offshore AI support region referenced in the DPA exchange for which no written legal basis, Controller/Processor designation or DPO is recorded, and the vendor request, minimised-export manifest and egress/access records are preserved. CSC concurs that only the minimised export may be used pending the four recorded conditions.

Passing the Bureau's request to REG/TDRA: the Bureau asks CSC to relay and preserve the vendor request, minimised-export manifest and egress/access records and to pass on any information identifying the owner of the flagged scheduled bulk upload; CSC holds no such record and asks REG/TDRA to identify the request owner so the transfer assessment can be completed, while the R2 999 record stays UNVERIFIED for window T+3 to T+10.

The excerpts do not answer what destination cloud region and provider, what categories and volume of subscriber data, what transfer mechanism and protection, or what written legal basis apply to the flagged scheduled bulk upload, nor whether it is the same cross-border movement as the vendor offshore AI support region; NOC, CSC and the Bureau each state they do not hold these details.

claim.statement: The KNOWLEDGE excerpts do not answer who is Controller and who is Processor for the vendor's offshore AI support region, nor the Article 23(1) basis for any full-identifier core log upload; the closest available UAE excerpts are telecom licensing provisions that do not address that designation.

data.description: Operator notifies the telecom regulator of an unplanned outage
Operator notifies emergency services that emergency calls fail

No rule in the excerpts requires an automated closed-loop optimiser change to core network configuration to pass a sandbox validation stage or a pre-deployment risk assessment before auto-approval; the CHG-1 ticket could set 'sandbox stage' to 'skipped' and be auto-approved with no human gate.

Auto-approval by the closed-loop optimiser left no identified accountable human owner or countersignatory for CHG-1; the excerpts define no role responsible for approving, or being accountable for, an automated change to core signalling configuration.

No rule requires sandbox/staged validation, or a pre-application hold, before a closed-loop optimiser's change to core signalling protection parameters is auto-approved and applied: CHG-1's 'sandbox stage' was skipped and the only preventative verb available to NOC (rollback_change) cannot operate on a change that has not yet been applied.

No accountable owner or human approver is defined for changes raised and auto-approved by the closed-loop network optimiser, and there is no separation between the system that raises a change and the system that approves it, so no role is answerable for CHG-1 before it applies.

No UAE text shown requires a sandbox validation stage and an explicit human authorisation gate before an autonomously generated change to core network resilience controls, such as a route-flood protection limit or route filter, is applied.

No UAE text shown sets a deadline for a licensee to report to TDRA an autonomously approved change whose rollback has failed, or a loss of core resilience protection, so the elapsed time before regulatory visibility is unbounded.

UAE has no rule requiring sandbox validation or a human authorisation gate before a closed-loop network optimiser applies changes that can affect emergency call routing; CHG-1 was auto-approved with the 'sandbox stage' skipped.

No deadline requires a licensee to notify the 999 emergency authority when a network change or outage may affect emergency call routing; here the authority learned of a possibly-applied, un-rollbackable change from a failed rollback rather than a mandated notification.

There is no rule requiring human authorisation or a pre-application sandbox/verification stage before an autonomous closed-loop optimiser applies a configuration change to core network routing, and no mechanism exists for me to hold or cancel a pending auto-approved change (the rollback verb only acts on a change that has already applied).

No owner is designated in the ticket or in the retrieved texts for confirming whether CHG-1 actually applied to core site A and for restoring the pre-change configuration after the rollback failed; the optimiser, the rollback tool and network telemetry each report a different version of element state with nobody accountable for resolving it.

No UAE text retrieved states a deadline for confirming the impact on 999/112 emergency call routing of a core-network change, or for notifying TDRA or the emergency authorities about such a change or any resulting outage; my licence text conditions duties on TDRA direction but sets no reporting clock.

There is no UAE rule in the available texts governing automated (closed-loop/AI-driven) network configuration change approval: nothing requires a sandbox validation stage to be executed, human authorisation to be obtained, or peer review before a change affecting emergency call routing or route-flood protection is committed.

No UAE text available sets a deadline for a licensee to establish and report the actual deployed state of a network element after a failed rollback or an unconfirmed change, nor a deadline for notifying TDRA once such a change might be live.

Ownership of oversight for AI/closed-loop network automation in telecommunications is not settled: it is unclear whether the regulator (TDRA) or the Federal Authority for Artificial Intelligence and Data owns the automated-decision aspects of a change such as CHG-1, and no allocation is stated in the available texts.

No owner is accountable for the applied configuration state of core site A: the rollback tool reported 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back' while EMS was told the element state is unconfirmed, so no named party can authoritatively state what configuration is live on the core.

There is no UAE telecom-sector rule that makes a sandbox/validation stage and human authorisation mandatory before an AI/closed-loop optimiser applies a change to a CII core network element, nor that bars skipping those stages as CHG-1 did.

No rule assigns a single owner for establishing whether an auto-approved change is actually live when the automated rollback reports 'no applied change', so change-ticket evidence, the operator's optimiser and network operations element state sit with different parties and each can assume the change was never applied.

No rule requires human authorisation, or completion of the sandbox validation stage, before a closed-loop optimiser applies changes to emergency-call path elements: CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped, lowered the route-flood limit and removed the inbound route filter on core site A, and its automated rollback failed.

No UAE deadline or maximum interval is set for confirming the live state of an emergency-call-path element after a failed automated rollback, nor for reporting degraded (rather than complete-loss) emergency call service; the state of core site A stayed UNCONFIRMED across successive notices while R2 999 routing showed no path.

No rule in the retrievable material requires human authorisation, or the completion of the sandbox stage, before a closed-loop network optimiser applies a change to a live core element: CHG-1 was auto-approved with the 'sandbox stage' field skipped and no human authorisation, and the closest UAE text on human oversight of automated decisions only requires a human element in reviewing automated processing decisions at the Data Subject's request.

The licence requires notification of an unplanned interruption 'as soon as possible' but fixes no deadline, threshold or trigger for when a partially confirmed outage becomes notifiable, so OpCo has no clock for acting on an event whose element state is unconfirmed (core site A isolated; 6 of 15 R2 sites unserved; CHG-1 applied state unknown).

No UAE text in the record requires sandbox validation and human authorisation before an automated or closed-loop change is applied to core network elements that carry emergency-call routing; change-control safeguards such as the sandbox stage, peer review and named human approval are left to the licensee's internal process, which here skipped the sandbox stage and auto-approved the change with no human authorisation.

The licence duty is timed only as 'as soon as possible': no UAE text in the record sets a numeric deadline for reporting an unplanned interruption to TDRA or for restoring service, so NOC's request for a regulator-held restoration and reporting timeframe cannot be answered from the texts available.

No UAE text in the record imposes an emergency-call-specific continuity duty, such as priority restoration of 999/112 routing, dedicated resilience requirements for emergency-call-routing elements, or penalty exposure, distinct from the general unplanned-interruption clause, even though the R2 impact was the loss of the 999 routing path.

No UAE rule requires human authorisation, customer-impact review, or completion of the sandbox/validation stage before an automated closed-loop optimiser applies a change to a critical core network element; CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation, and the change removed a protection limit and an inbound route filter on a core site.

The operator licence requires notification of an unplanned interruption only 'as soon as possible', with no fixed timeframe, no severity threshold and no separate rule for outages affecting emergency call routing, so an outage that removed R2's 999 path has no defined notification clock or reporting threshold.

No UAE text assigns an owner for asserting the applied configuration state of an automated change, or for reconciling digital-twin state with physical element state, when an auto-rollback fails; NOC twin metrics showed R2 emergency reachable and 100% sites served while CHG-1's state on core site A was unconfirmed.

No UAE instrument in the excerpts assigns an owner or a required verification step for confirming that 999 emergency call routing is actually restored on the real network (rather than in a telemetry/twin model) or for confirming the applied element state of a change on an emergency-call-path element before the incident is closed.

There is no UAE rule requiring human authorisation, sandbox validation or staged release before a closed-loop network optimiser applies a change to core network elements; CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped and went straight to a production core site.

No owner or system of record exists for confirming the applied configuration state of an automated network change: the optimiser applied (or did not apply) CHG-1 and the rollback tool reported 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back', leaving element state unconfirmed across NOC, EMS and CSC.

UAE telecom rules contain no requirement for sandbox validation, staged rollout or human authorisation before an automated closed-loop network optimiser applies a change that can affect core routing or emergency-call routing; the only relevant duty is retrospective notification after an interruption has occurred.

Licence clause 12.9.2 requires the Licensee to inform TDRA 'as soon as possible' and to state its own resolution time frames, but sets no fixed regulatory reporting deadline and no maximum restoration time for unplanned interruptions, so NOC's request for a regulator-held reporting or restoration timeframe has no UAE source.

No UAE text assigns a named owner for verifying the element-level applied configuration on a core site after a change, or for confirming real-network emergency reachability as distinct from operator telemetry twin metrics; in this incident the operator, the NOC, the emergency services sector and TDRA each hold part of the picture with none accountable for the confirmation.

No UAE text shown imposes a duty on the licensee to notify the 999 emergency call service (or NCEMA) directly when a change or outage affects emergency-call routing, or to verify restoration of emergency call reachability on the real network before declaring recovery; the only notification duty in the excerpts runs to subscribers, not to the emergency call service.

No text shown assigns ownership for confirming real-network emergency call reachability: NOC holds monitoring/twin telemetry, OpCo holds element-level applied state (unconfirmed after the failed CHG-1 rollback), and the 999 centre holds real call data, with no rule stating whose evidence governs a stand-down or restoration declaration.

No UAE rule requires a completed sandbox stage or human authorisation before a closed-loop network optimiser auto-approves a change touching core or emergency-call-routing elements: CHG-1 lowered the route-flood protection limit 100->50, removed the inbound route filter and skipped the sandbox with no human authorisation.

No rule requires a restoration claim to be verified on the real network before emergency reachability is declared restored or a public alert is stood down: OpCo's twin metrics (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) conflict with the 999 centre's report that R2 call volume has fallen to near zero.

There is no UAE rule requiring human authorisation and mandatory sandbox validation before an automated or AI-driven closed-loop network optimiser applies a change to core network elements or to any element in the emergency-call routing path; the CHG-1 ticket recorded 'sandbox stage: skipped' and was auto-approved with no human authorisation.

No rule assigns ownership of the control that can suspend, block or authorise the closed-loop optimiser's automated change approvals; NOC states it has no mandate verb to suspend the optimiser or block further auto-approved changes and asks REG to direct the suspension and to say who owns that control.

There is no UAE rule requiring the state of the real network to be reconciled with, and to prevail over, the digital-twin/telemetry state before restoration is declared: twin metrics report emergency_reachable.R2 = true and pct_sites_served = 100.0 while the 999 centre reports R2 call volume near zero, and the element-level applied state of CHG-1 is unconfirmable because the change system holds no applied record.

No rule requires the licensee to notify the emergency call centre / PSAP promptly during an incident affecting 999 routing: the 999 centre observed R2 call volume collapse and failing emergency calls, and states that no operator has contacted the centre.

There is no enforceable rule requiring human authorisation and a non-skippable sandbox/validation stage before an automated closed-loop function changes parameters on a core element that carries emergency call traffic; CHG-1 was auto-approved by the optimiser with the sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation, and the incident shows the policy expectation alone did not prevent it.

No actor is assigned to alert the emergency call service: EMS reports that no operator has contacted the 999 centre even after R2 lost its 999 routing path, and REG/NOC closed on wilt metrics without confirmation from the emergency service; UAE texts designate Emergency services as a critical sector but assign no owner for emergency-centre notification.

Two authoritative data sources conflict on whether emergency service is restored and no UAE text defines which measurement proves restoration of emergency call service or requires end-to-end verification with the emergency service: NOC reports emergency_reachable.R2=true and 100.0% sites served, while the 999 centre observes call volume from R2 near zero.

No UAE rule shown here requires human authorisation, or a completed sandbox/validation stage, before a closed-loop optimiser auto-approves a change to core network elements that carry emergency call routing.

No UAE rule shown here requires real-network confirmation of emergency call delivery, rather than digital twin or telemetry metrics, before a network operator declares emergency call routing restored and closes the incident.

There is no UAE rule requiring human authorisation, or a mandatory sandbox/validation stage, before an automated closed-loop network change that touches core or emergency-call-routing elements is applied; CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation.

No institution or role is identified as owning the control to suspend or block OpCo's auto-approving closed-loop optimiser for core/emergency-impacting changes; NOC states it has no mandate verb to suspend the optimiser or block auto-approved changes and asks TDRA to direct suspension and say who owns that control.

There is no UAE deadline for confirming the applied/element state of a change, for verifying real-network emergency reachability, or for reporting restoration after an unplanned interruption; Licence 12.9.2 requires only 'as soon as possible' and NOC asks TDRA for any regulator-held restoration or reporting timeframe.

No UAE rule requires human authorisation or a mandatory sandbox/validation stage before an automated closed-loop change alters core network or emergency-call-routing elements: CHG-1 removed the inbound route filter and lowered the route-flood protection limit on core site A with its 'sandbox stage' skipped, auto-approved, and without human authorisation.

No UAE rule specifies what evidence establishes that emergency call reachability has been restored: OpCo's Licence 12.9.2 notification and NOC twin metrics (emergency_reachable.R2=true, 100% sites served) declare restoration while the 999 centre's real-network data show R2 999 volume near zero, with no rule on which source governs or on real-network end-to-end verification before a 'restored' status is issued.

No owner is identified in the UAE framework for the control that suspends or blocks further auto-approved closed-loop changes touching core or emergency-call-routing elements: NOC states it has no mandate verb to suspend the optimiser or block further auto-approved changes and asks REG to direct suspension and to say who owns that control.

CHG-1 was auto-approved by a closed-loop network optimiser with the sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation, yet it touched core/emergency-call-routing elements; there is no rule requiring human authorisation or a mandatory sandbox for changes that can affect emergency call delivery.

Twin/synthetic metrics reported emergency_reachable.R2=true and 100% sites served while the 999 centre saw R2-origin 999 volume near zero; there is no rule requiring real-network end-to-end confirmation of emergency call delivery instead of reliance on twin metrics.

No owner or rule covers verifying the applied element-level state of a change: the rollback tool returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back' even though the change evidently took effect (core site A isolated), leaving the live configuration state unconfirmed and unattributed.

No UAE instrument in this record requires human authorisation, a completed sandbox validation stage, or an emergency-impact gate before an AI/closed-loop optimiser applies a configuration change to core or emergency-call-routing network elements.

No UAE text in this record assigns an owner for the control that suspends or blocks further auto-approved closed-loop network changes: NOC states it has no mandate verb to suspend the optimiser or block auto-approved changes and asks REG to say who owns that control.

Licence 12.9.2 requires notification 'as soon as possible' and disclosure of the time frames for resolution but sets no numeric deadline for the operator's notification or for reporting restoration, so no regulator-held restoration or reporting timeframe exists to answer NOC's request.

No UAE text in this record specifies what evidence proves that an unplanned interruption affecting emergency-call routing is resolved; the incident shows telemetry twin metrics (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) contradicting real-network data (R2 999 call volume near zero for about 7 minutes) with no rule on which prevails.

There is no UAE rule requiring explicit human authorisation, or a mandatory non-skippable validation stage, before an AI- or optimiser-driven closed-loop change alters core network or emergency-call-routing elements; the optimiser was able to remove an inbound route filter and lower route-flood protection unattended.

Ownership of the control to suspend an operator's closed-loop optimiser, or to block further auto-approved changes touching core and emergency-call-routing elements, is unassigned: NOC states it has no such mandate verb and asks REG to direct it, while CSC's mandate holds only notify, issue_advisory and request_ioc.

Conflicting evidence standards co-exist for declaring emergency-call reachability restored: OpCo's digital-twin metrics report emergency_reachable.R2=true and 100% sites served, while the 999 centre's real-network call records show R2 volume near zero; no UAE text states which evidence discharges restoration of emergency services.

No UAE deadline exists for an operator to establish and report the applied configuration state of a change whose automated rollback failed, nor for reporting real-network emergency-reachability outcomes after a divergence is detected.

No rule requires human authorisation, a completed sandbox stage or an emergency-element safeguard before an automated closed-loop change is applied to core or emergency-call-routing elements: CHG-1 was auto-approved with 'sandbox stage: skipped' and no human authorisation, and removing the inbound route filter on core site A took R2's 999 path down.

No owner is identified for the authority that auto-approves closed-loop changes touching core and emergency-call-routing elements: CSC requires REG to state who owns that control before any further such change is applied, so decision rights currently sit with an automated optimiser with no named accountable human.

Where a twin/metrics view reports full emergency reachability (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) while the 999 centre reports R2 999 call volume near zero and failed calls, no rule states which source discharges an emergency-reachability confirmation, so the incident could have been closed on metrics alone.

No UAE text available here requires human authorisation or mandatory sandbox validation before an automated closed-loop change is applied to core or emergency-call-routing elements; CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation, and nothing in the excerpts states a rule that forbids it.

No UAE text available here designates the owner of the authority to suspend or block autonomous closed-loop change authority on core or emergency-call-routing elements; NOC states it has no mandate verb to suspend the optimiser or block further auto-approved changes and asks who owns that control, while no excerpt names an owner.

No UAE text available here sets a restoration or reporting timeframe for an unplanned interruption affecting emergency call routing; NOC asked for 'any regulator-held requirement or timeframe for restoration and reporting' and no excerpt supplies one.

No UAE text available here requires restoration of emergency call reachability to be evidenced end-to-end on the real network rather than by digital-twin or synthetic telemetry; the operator's twin metrics report emergency_reachable.R2 = true and 100% sites served while the 999 centre records R2 call volume near zero.

The excerpts allocate record-keeping to the 'Controller' and 'Processor' and require a DPO for high-risk or large-volume processing, but nothing before me fixes who is Controller and who is Processor, or who appoints the DPO, when a network vendor runs an offshore AI fault-diagnosis model over the operator's subscriber data; NOC's request for controller/processor and DPO arrangements cannot be answered from the text.

The shown UAE text lets personal data go outside the State on a contract or on consent alone and requires no data protection impact assessment and no prior consultation with the Bureau before a transfer; there is therefore no express pre-transfer review step for sending subscriber data to a vendor-hosted offshore AI region.

No UAE excerpt sets conditions for using live subscriber identifiers in AI-based fault diagnosis, for minimising such data, or for human review of the AI's output; the operator is left to decide on its own whether to train and run the diagnosis model on live personal data rather than on simulated data.

No UAE text in the excerpts assigns an owner for suspending a closed-loop network optimiser or for blocking further auto-approved changes that touch core or emergency-call-routing elements; NOC states it has no mandate verb to do so and has asked REG to direct suspension and name the owner, and that question remained unanswered at T+20.

No UAE text in the excerpts requires sandbox validation or human authorisation before a closed-loop optimiser auto-approves a change affecting core or emergency-call-routing elements; CHG-1 skipped the sandbox stage and was auto-approved with no human authorisation, and CSC has required OpCo to explain how that was possible.

No UAE text in the excerpts sets a deadline for establishing the element-level applied state of a change after a failed rollback, or for confirming end-to-end real-network 999 reachability after an emergency-call-routing outage; at T+20 the applied state of CHG-1 on core site A still cannot be determined.

Two evidence standards conflict on whether R2 emergency service is restored: OpCo twin metrics report emergency_reachable.R2=true and pct_sites_served=100.0 after wilting to core site B, while the 999 centre's real call data shows R2 999 volume near zero for about seven minutes and no UAE text in the excerpts states which evidence discharges a restoration claim.

No UAE rule or standard states whether digital-twin or simulated network metrics may be used to confirm emergency-call reachability or restoration to the regulator; in this incident twin metrics reported emergency_reachable.R2=true and 100% sites served while the 999 centre recorded near-zero R2 999 call volume and unverified reachability.

No party in the incident can name the owner of the authority to approve, block or suspend auto-approved closed-loop network changes that touch core or emergency-call-routing elements; NOC states it has no mandate verb for this, and both NOC and CSC ask REG to state who owns that control.

There is no UAE rule in scope requiring sandbox validation and human authorisation before an automated closed-loop change is applied to core or emergency-call-routing elements; CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation.

Two sources of truth for emergency-service restoration conflict and no UAE text states which governs: OpCo's twin metrics report emergency_reachable.R2 = true and pct_sites_served = 100.0, while the 999 centre records R2-origin 999 volume near zero for about 7 minutes with social-media reports of failed 999 calls.

There is no UAE instrument, in the excerpts available, that expressly requires sandbox validation and named human authorisation before an AI/closed-loop network optimiser applies a change to core network or emergency-call-routing elements; CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation.

UAE texts, as retrieved, give no rule resolving a direct conflict between digital-twin metrics claiming restoration and real-network 999 call-volume evidence, and no rule stating that twin/simulation metrics cannot discharge end-to-end emergency-call reachability confirmation.

No owner is designated in the available texts for the authority to suspend or re-authorise an auto-approved closed-loop change touching core or emergency-call-routing elements; NOC states it has no such verb and asks REG to say who owns that control.

No UAE licence condition or instrument requires a sandbox stage, human authorisation or a named authoriser before a closed-loop network optimiser applies a change to core or emergency-call-routing elements; the closest duty is post-hoc notification of the resulting interruption, which is why CHG-1 could be auto-approved with 'sandbox stage: skipped' and no human authorisation.

No UAE text requires an operator to verify emergency-call reachability on the real network, as distinct from digital-twin telemetry, before declaring restoration; the twin reported emergency_reachable.R2=true / pct_sites_served=100.0 while the 999 centre saw R2 call volume near zero, and only the regulator and the 999 centre imposed real-network confirmation.

No owner is designated for the vendor's offshore AI processing of OpCo subscriber data: the DPA has had to ask OpCo to confirm in writing who is Controller and who is Processor for that region and to appoint or confirm a DPO, although the incident record itself is owned by NOC and the transfer was requested directly by the vendor.

No UAE instrument retrieved designates who owns the authority to authorise, suspend or block automated (closed-loop) network changes that touch core or emergency-call-routing elements. CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation, NOC states it has no mandate verb to suspend the pipeline, and no party in the incident could name the control owner.

No UAE rule retrieved requires human authorisation or mandatory sandbox/staged validation before an automated change is applied to core or emergency-call-routing elements. CHG-1 lowered the route-flood protection limit (100->50) and removed the inbound route filter on core site A with the ticket field 'sandbox stage': skipped and no human authorisation.

No UAE rule retrieved requires a licensee to be able to determine and evidence the applied configuration state of core network elements after an automated change, or to hold a verified rollback path. The CHG-1 rollback returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back', a later attempt returned done with twin metrics 'no change', and the applied state of core site A cannot be determined.

No UAE rule retrieved requires end-to-end real-network verification of emergency call delivery, rather than telemetry or digital-twin metrics, before an operator declares an emergency-services outage resolved. NOC reported emergency_reachable.R2=true and pct_sites_served=100.0 while the 999 centre recorded R2-origin 999 call volume near zero for about 7 minutes.

No owner is designated for determining and recording who is Controller and who is Processor for the vendor's offshore AI support region, nor for appointing or confirming the DPO required for the new-technology, high-volume automated processing; NOC states those designations are outside its authority and are being raised to the accountable function.

The UAE PDPL excerpts provide a right to information about automated processing decisions but do not set a specific human-oversight or review rule for an offshore AI diagnosis model processing subscriber logs; NOC has flagged this as new-technology, high-volume automated processing.

No UAE instrument retrieved designates the accountable owner of the authority to approve or suspend auto-approved closed-loop optimiser changes touching core or emergency-call-routing elements: TDRA records the owner as unnamed and requires the licensee to name it, while NOC states it has no mandate verb to suspend the optimiser or block further auto-approved changes. The CIIP framework and the AI policy state governance and human-oversight requirements but name no responsible change authority for this class of automated action.

There is no operational UAE rule, in the retrieved texts, governing the cross-border transfer of subscriber-level data from an operator's core network to a cloud region outside the UAE: the PDPL Implementing Regulations that would operationalise legal basis and cross-border transfers have still not been issued and no supervisory authority has been unambiguously designated for private sector oversight, so the flagged bulk upload cannot be tested against a published UAE transfer rule.

No UAE rule requires human authorisation, or completion of a validation stage, before an automated closed-loop optimiser changes configuration that touches core or emergency-call-routing elements: CHG-1 was auto-approved with the 'sandbox stage' skipped and no human authorisation, and it lowered the route-flood protection limit on core site A from 100 to 50 and removed the inbound route filter.

No owner is designated for the auto-approved closed-loop change authority over emergency-call-routing elements: NOC states it has no mandate verb to suspend the optimiser or block further auto-approved changes, REG had to ask who owns that control, and TDRA named OpCo as accountable only after the incident.

No UAE rule states how an operator's digital-twin telemetry (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) relates to real-network evidence for emergency call reachability, so nothing makes confirmed end-to-end delivery of real 999 calls, rather than twin metrics, the governing test for declaring restoration.

No rule requires human authorisation, or completion of the sandbox stage, before an automated closed-loop optimiser applies changes to core elements that carry emergency-call routing; nor is there a rule requiring independent verification of the applied element state when the automated rollback reports that there is no applied change to roll back.

There is no UAE rule requiring sandbox validation and explicit human authorisation before an automated closed-loop optimiser applies a change to core or emergency-call-routing elements; the change here skipped the sandbox stage and had no human authorisation.

No deadline applies for establishing and stating the element-level applied state of a change that cannot be rolled back or confirmed, so CHG-1's applied state on core site A remained undetermined across the whole incident window with no clock running.

No function is designated as owner of the Controller/Processor determination and the DPO appointment for the vendor's offshore AI support region; NOC states that designation sits outside its authority and is 'being raised to the accountable function', leaving the ownership unassigned.

There is no UAE rule or standard specific to uploading telecom core logs containing subscriber identifiers to an offshore AI-model support region; the closest provision is the general Article 23(1)(a) contract route, which does not address AI-model analysis or vendor technical safeguards.

No UAE instrument retrieved designates who owns the authority to approve closed-loop / AI-optimiser changes on core or emergency-call-routing elements: TDRA records that no UAE instrument retrieved designates that owner, that the operator's NOC merely records OpCo as accountable, and that the owner must be named formally by the licensee - leaving approval authority for emergency-affecting automated change undefined during an active 999 incident.

No UAE instrument retrieved requires human authorisation and a completed sandbox/validation stage before an auto-approved closed-loop optimiser change is applied to core or emergency-call-routing elements; CHG-1 was applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped and no human authorisation, and the requirement has had to be imposed after the fact by TDRA direction.

No UAE rule retrieved states that real-network end-to-end delivery must be proven before an emergency-call-routing outage is treated as restored, or that digital-twin/simulation metrics do not discharge that confirmation; twin metrics reported emergency_reachable.R2 = true and pct_sites_served = 100.0 while the 999 centre's real-network record showed R2 999 volume near zero, and the closure test had to be supplied by TDRA direction.

No rule in what I hold assigns an owner for the authority to auto-approve closed-loop network changes that touch core or emergency-call-routing elements. CHG-1 was auto-approved by the optimiser with the sandbox stage skipped and no human authorisation; TDRA/REG had to direct OpCo to suspend such changes pending review and to name the accountable owner, and CSC asked REG to state who owns that control. The closest UAE text governs high-risk new-technology processing generally but nothing addresses automated network change authority.

OpCo's twin telemetry asserts emergency_reachable.R2=true and pct_sites_served=100.0 after R2 was wilted onto core site B, while 999-centre real-network data for the same region and window shows 999 volume near zero and failed calls. No rule I hold says which evidence discharges a restoration claim or how a twin-versus-real-network conflict is resolved, so R2 999 reachability stays UNVERIFIED.

Neither TDRA's direction nor the DPA/Bureau assessment states a deadline for OpCo to state the applied configuration state of core site A, to complete the Article 23(1) basis and the Controller/Processor/DPO designations, or to produce the special record; the record duty is expressed only as submission whenever requested.
